items.excerpt: MiniMax H3 的 pi-H3 加速包：初步测试记录 一句话结论：在一张 12 GB 显卡上，pi-H3 2 步 + DWD 比官方 4 步加速 LoRA 快 1.9 倍 （68 s vs 130 s）， 4 步快 1.55 倍 （84 s vs 130 s）；肉眼觉得最好的是 pi-H3 4 步 ，但样本只有几个种子，只能当参考。 另有一个和速度无关的意外结果，见第五节末尾。 一、起因 MiniMax H3 发布之后，好几种地方都在推它的加速方案。就顺手做了一轮 冒烟测试 —— 不是横评，是想先搞清楚「这东西在我的卡上到底跑多快、画面能不能看、和官方 LoRA 差多少」。 先说清楚性质： 单条提示词、每种配置只出 1 个视频（换了 1 个 seed 复跑）、没有重复采样 。 下面的秒数是实测，画质部分是主观判断 + 一个粗糙的客观指标。 二、pi-H3 是什么 MiniMax H3 是原生「视频 + 音频」一起生成的视频大模型。pi-H3 是在它之上做的 少步数蒸馏 adapter ， 两个卖点： 2 步或 4 步出片 （H3 原始采样要几十步） DWD = Decoding Without a Decoder ：最后一步直接从 latent 预测像素， 整个视频 VAE 解码被跳过 （音频 VAE 还是要的） 形式是 LoRA 权重（放在 models/loras/ ）…

items.title: 高危漏洞 Upload2Shell 公开：上传图片即可入侵服务器｜CVE-2026-125396，8.5 分
items.excerpt: 一个普通的图片上传功能，竟然可能成为攻击者控制服务器的入口。 近日，安全研究人员公开了名为 Upload2Shell 的高危漏洞研究，影响范围极广，涉及 WordPress、Roundcube 网页邮箱、MediaWiki、DokuWiki、CUPS 打印服务，以及广泛使用的图像处理工具 Pillow、ImageMagick。就连 Google 的部分文件处理服务，Debian、Ubuntu 等 Linux 发行版也受到影响。 此外，ComfyUI、Stable Diffusion WebUI 等热门 AI 绘图工具也被发现存在潜在的漏洞触发路径。 Upload2Shell 是什么？ 漏洞的根源来自 Ghostscript ，一款拥有数十年历史的开源 PDF 和 PostScript 文件处理工具。 很多软件在生成图片缩略图、预览 PDF、转换文档、处理打印任务时，都会在后台调用 Ghostscript。 研究人员发现，通过特制文件，可以突破 Ghostscript 的安全沙箱，在服务器上执行任意命令。更麻烦的是，即使上传文件的扩展名是 .jpg 或 .png ，在特定的文件处理流程中也可能触发漏洞。 漏洞名称：Upload2Shell 漏洞编号：CVE-2026-125396 漏洞评分：CVSS 4.0 8.5/10（高危） 发现时间：2026 年 7 月 27 日 技术细节公…

items.excerpt: 报名从速｜来MEET2027！听AI前沿实践者交出“判断” 量子位的朋友们 2026-11-24 11:33:48 来源： 量子位 12.9 北京，来MEET2027现场 2026年，AI领域最显著的变化发生在交付现场：模型开始接手任务，机器人离开舞台走进产线，智能体被嵌进组织的日常流程。这些事分散在不同行业与场景里，我们却从中看到了同一条线索。 12月9日，量子位主办的 MEET2027智能未来大会 将在北京·金茂万丽酒店举行。大会以 “智行合一·驭见未来” 为主题，在一整天的时间里，邀请AI领域的一线代表共同来回答：当AI从模型能力变成可交付的系统产出，是谁在把它送进真实场景，又是谁在底层为它提供支撑？ 一次关于“能干”的重估 智能体从聊天走向作业，能自主拆解目标、调度工具、跨系统跑完长链条任务；具身智能给模型配上身体，让机器人在充满意外的真实场景里学会感知与操作；世界模型与空间智能把虚实两头接通，机器动手之前先把因果弄明白。也正因如此，当智能开始承担决策和执行， 可靠、可控、可解释 就从技术议题变成了公共议题， 这正是本届大会主题 「智行合一·驭见未来」 的由来。“智行合一”，说的是理解、规划、执行、反馈这些过去分散在多套系统里的环节，如今被压进同一个闭环；“驭见未来”，是因为未来不会自己走过来给人看，它得有人驾驭—— 谁能驾驭它，谁才有资格谈下一个十年。 一场关于“落地”…

items.title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit
items.excerpt: Node affinity prediction in the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB) asks how a node's future interactions will be distributed over other nodes. On this task, methods that reuse past ground-truth labels often outperform temporal graph neural networks, and the state of the art builds on them. Such comparisons assume a point-in-time correct evaluation, in which a model receives only information available at prediction time. items.title: Fast 4-bit KV-Cache Decoding on Hopper GPUs: Why Existing Kernels Are Slow and How to Fix Them
items.excerpt: A 4-bit KV cache reads about half the bytes of FP8, but Hopper GPUs have no FP4 hardware and little instruction-issue capacity per byte of memory bandwidth, so 4-bit values must be decoded in software. On H200, vLLM's NVFP4 KV path (FlashInfer's decode) reaches 10-20% of memory bandwidth and is up to 1.7x slower than FP8. NVBit instruction counts show two causes: the kernels behind vLLM's 4-bit paths (FlashInfer NVFP4, Triton UltraQuant) execute 2-6x Hopper's issue budget per byte and serialize loading, decoding and matrix multiplies. items.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks
items.excerpt: Staff pseudonymizing financial data in closed networks must interpret abbreviated column names, identify personal information, and choose processing methods. Local language models can assist, but may give different labels for the same input. PseuDRAGON keeps confirmed judgments and corrections outside a fixed model and reuses them through exact-name lookup and learned rules. For expert review, the workflow searches institutional policy, national privacy law, then international sources. items.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
items.excerpt: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. items.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
items.excerpt: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. items.title: RepoClean: Evaluating Coding Agents on Repository-Level Obsolete Code Cleanup
items.excerpt: Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong repository-level programming capabilities. However, as software evolves, repository code may become redundant or obsolete, increasing maintenance costs and potentially introducing functional issues. Agents must therefore identify and remove unnecessary code safely, yet autonomous repository-level code cleanup remains insufficiently evaluated in isolation. items.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
items.excerpt: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems.
